title: Design a streaming path through CDN, proxy and server
businessContext: Suspense works locally but users receive the entire response only after the slow report finishes.
problemStatement: Design the system for Three network hops; p95 useful shell under 400 ms; report data may take 3 seconds. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Contain dependency failures without leaking private data.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Three network hops; p95 useful shell under 400 ms; report data may take 3 seconds
functional: Contain dependency failures without leaking private data.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Place boundaries below the layouts shared by the relevant navigation, then start only necessary independent work.

After streaming begins, the server cannot reliably replace the committed HTTP status with a later error. Use proper error boundaries and correlation, and avoid promising a 404/500 status from an already-committed successful stream.
alternativeApproaches: It can reveal a buffering symptom but is not a complete delivery design. Compare supported proxy settings, payload sizes and actual browser performance before accepting a bandwidth or CPU regression.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Use a controlled delayed child and capture chunk arrival at each hop.
Compare direct loads and sibling client transitions.
Break a late dependency and inspect visible recovery, logs and final response status.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
